title: BEACON Early Action Protocol (EAP)
description: Validates config/eap/*.json — one IFRC-structured Early Action Protocol per file (ADR-034 §1, FR-AA-1, ADR-012 config-not-code). All SIX IFRC EAP elements are required: the two-stage trigger (triggers.readiness + triggers.activation), the pre-agreed action list (actions), the pre-arranged resource ceiling (resourceCeiling), the roles/activation mechanism (approval), the geographic scope (scope) and the STOP mechanism (stop). `stop` is REQUIRED, not optional: an EAP that cannot be stopped is the dangerous case. DATA-NOT-CODE is enforced here, not asserted: every string is either a closed enum, a slug pattern, or `safeProse` — a character allow-list that admits no `/`, `$`, `{`, `}`, backtick, `<`, `>`, `\`, `|`, `#`, `=`, `*`, `?`, `!`, and no `..`. There is therefore no expression, template, path or URL anywhere in an EAP for an eval/Function/dynamic-import to consume, and an EAP id can never become a path segment.

status.description: The only admissible value today. Every shipped EAP is a demonstration artifact; approving a real protocol is a National-Society/authority act that BEACON does not perform, so no `ENDORSED` value exists to claim (ADR-034 honest limitation 2).

allOf.description: Every shipped EAP must state, in its own file, that it is not approved or endorsed by any National Society, hydromet service or civil-protection authority.

resourceCeiling.description: The PRE-ARRANGED ceiling. There is deliberately no monetary/donor/budget field: BEACON holds no financial data and inventing one would be an unsourced figure (ADR-035 §4 PERMANENTLY-OUT).

approval.description: Roles / activation mechanism. The fallback WIDENS who may approve after a delay; it never removes the requirement for approval (ADR-034 §6, FST-4).

stop.description: The STOP mechanism — REQUIRED. `maxDurationHours` is the machine-enforceable half (pure clock arithmetic, so an activation cannot outlive it); `conditions[]` are the human-observed halves, and only a declared condition id may be cited when stopping.

authorizerRole.description: APPROVER_ROLES (src/domain/governance.ts) — the one vocabulary for who may approve. PUBLIC and RESPONDER are excluded: an unauthenticated or non-approving principal can never authorize or stop a protocol (Art. XIII).

trigger.description: One stage of the two-stage trigger. BOTH magnitude gates are required so no stage can ship ungated: `minMembersFraction` gates ENSEMBLE_MEMBER_COUNT evidence (share of members over `threshold`), `minLikelihoodClass` gates SOURCE_DERIVED_PROBABILITY evidence via the ADR-033 classifier. The two evidence kinds are never converted into one another.

resourceKind.description: Mirrors RESOURCE_KINDS (src/domain/resource.ts). JSON Schema cannot import a TypeScript constant, so this is the one copy that can drift — it is PINNED to RESOURCE_KINDS by tests/architecture/domain-db-enum-pin.test.ts (arm 4). 'TEAM' is FR-D6-1 (ADR-035 §4): an EAP may pre-position a volunteer team exactly as it pre-positions any other resource kind.

polygon.description: A GeoJSON Polygon (RFC 7946). Only Polygon is admitted: a scope must be a closed area, and admitting a Point/LineString would let a scope be un-intersectable. There is no `geometryRef` indirection — a reference would be a path, and paths are exactly what this schema refuses.
